t: Section 48102(a)(9) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(9) $124,093,750 for the period beginning on October 1, 2015, and ending on July 15, 2016.”.

fable.w: This section only amends a statutory provision to set an authorized funding amount for a specified period. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government, so there is no tempting participation reading.

opus.w: The section only changes a funding amount in 49 U.S.C. 48102(a)(9) for the period from October 1, 2015, to July 15, 2016. It does not mention consultation, comment periods, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue. Being a formal amendment to the Code is not enough to count as participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a straightforward appropriation amendment that sets a specific funding amount for a defined period. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The text contains no reference to participation by non-federal parties in any decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 48102(a)(9) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(9) $124,093,750 for the period beginning on October 1, 2015, and ending on July 15, 2016.”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this is an amendment to a statute, it implies some legislative process involving public input. However, the text itself is purely a fiscal appropriation amendment. It does not describe any process for public comment, consultation, or participation. It simply sets a dollar amount for a specific time period.
